Conveniently add Icon Attributions to a Leaflet Map

Source: R/layers.R
addIconAttribution.Rd

Adds a short character string to the bottom-right of the map widget with the attribution and license of an icon library. group and layerId can be used to add or remove the attribution - e.g., if the markers using magicIcons() are hidden.

Usage

addIconAttribution(map, library = "fontawesome", layerId = NULL, group = NULL)

Arguments

map

a map widget object created from leaflet()

library

One of "fontawesome", "bootstrap", "ionicons", or "lucide" defining the icon library of interest. Defaults to "fontawesome". Alternatively, "text" shows icon as text, which is useful for numbered or lettered markers (e.g., icon = 1:10). Text is bold and shrinks to fit, so is best kept to around three characters. "svg" uses icon as raw SVG markup (e.g., '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">...</svg>'), so any icon can be used. Parts of the SVG which use currentColor or have no fill of their own take on iconColor. Only use SVG markup you trust, as it is inserted directly into legends.

layerId

the layer id

group

the name of the group the newly created layers should belong to (for clearGroup() and addLayersControl() purposes). Human-friendly group names are permitted–they need not be short, identifier-style names. Any number of layers and even different types of layers (e.g., markers and polygons) can share the same group name.

Value

a leaflet widget

Examples

library(leaflet)
leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    icon = magicIcons("industry"),
    group = "Sites"
  ) |>
  addIconAttribution(group = "Sites") |>
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = "Sites")
